messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xxs from serving cluster rack-3 (serving-t4-rack3). Autoscale triggered, but we're seeing CUDA OOMs and container restarts. Metric highlights: p95 latency +420ms, error rate 18% across model-route /v1/generate. Creating incident INC-2026-2345. @here

elena: acked, I'm paging on-call. seeing repeated RDMA timeouts from node gp-node-23 and 24 in the logs.

raj: oncall responding, joining. any immediate customer impact?

support-bot: Customer impact: 3 customers reporting degraded responses (high latency, partial outputs). No full data exfiltration. Tickets: CS-5123, CS-5124.

elena: quick triage — top errors from runtime logs: `CUDA out of memory` inside container, but dmesg on host shows IB link flaps and 'rdma_cm: timed out waiting for connect' earlier. suspect packet loss on IB fabric causing streaming KVs to fail and runtime to exhaust memory.

maya: logs pasted: ```
[2026-03-15T09:11:02Z] serving: kv_cache_fetch failed: rdma_read error -62
[2026-03-15T09:11:03Z] runtime: async write failed: -110 (ETIMEDOUT)
[2026-03-15T09:11:04Z] gpu0: CUDA error: out of memory
[2026-03-15T09:11:05Z] container: restart (OOM)
```

tom: running `ibv_devinfo` and `ibstat` on gp-node-23: physical port reports 'Link Down' intermittently. switch logs show flaps on port 42/43.

jordan: adding infra team. tagging network-owner @raj for fabric checks.

raj: I'm on fabric. immediate mitigation plan: 1) drain traffic from gp-node-23/24, 2) failover serving shards to rack-1 replicas, 3) apply per-route rate limits to affected customers to reduce pressure, 4) if flaps persist, run link bounce and put node in maintenance.

elena: I'm starting drain: `kubectl cordon gp-node-23 && kubectl drain gp-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --force --grace-period=30` — doing one node at a time to avoid overload.

maya: triggered fallback policy for model-route /v1/generate -> routes to smaller-quantized variant (quant-v2) to reduce GPU memory pressure.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident INC-2026-2345 assigned to elena (primary) and raj (secondary). Priority P1. Escalation timer started.

tom: after draining gp-node-23, error rate dropped ~9% within 90s. p95 reduced by ~200ms but still above SLO. 

raj: switch team confirmed intermittent packet drops on inter-rack fabric between rack-3 top-of-rack (ToR-3A) and spine-2. There's a microburst/ECN event, likely queue overflow. I'm putting affected ports in errdisable to stop flapping while we investigate.

elena: rolling restart of ml-runtime on failover nodes to ensure clean KV cache warmup. Monitoring for new OOMs.

maya: notes: we saw KV cache thrash — repeated re-fetches due to RDMA read failures caused memory growth in the runtime's prefetch queue; combined with sustained batch sizes, CUDA OOMs triggered. Need long-term fix: backpressure on KV fetch + reduce prefetch concurrency.

jordan: customer-impact update: notifying CS to send template: "We are experiencing degraded LLM response quality and latency due to network disruption affecting inference routing. Mitigations are in progress; we'll follow up in 1 hour or sooner." @support-bot please send.

support-bot: Sent update to affected customers (CS-5123, CS-5124).

raj: temporary fabric mitigations applied: rate-limit ECN marking disabled on ToR-3A egress, increased buffer for the problematic ports, and isolated flapping port. Will monitor for 10m.

tom: infra observation: after isolation p99 latencies fell ~300ms, error rate to 4.2%. Some nodes still report one-off CUDA memory warnings during cold KV fetches.

elena: handoff: I'm nearing the end of my pager window; handing to raj. Summary for on-call: INCIDENT INC-2026-2345 — RDMA packet loss caused KV fetch retries, runtime prefetch queue increased, leading to CUDA OOM and container restarts on gp-node-23/24. Mitigations applied: drained nodes, rerouted shards to rack-1, fallback model routing, switch port isolation and buffer adjustments. Current status: degraded but stabilizing. Please watch for recurring flaps and any new OOMs.

raj: taking over. I'll stay on until fabric fully stable and a postmortem action list drafted. Next steps: coordinate with network vendor for switch telemetry, add runtime backpressure change to POSTMORTEM PR, and propose a short-term autoscale throttle for prefetch concurrency.

maya: quick repro note for the postmortem: add a synthetic test that simulates RDMA transient failures and verifies runtime prefetch cap prevents mem spike.

jordan: assigning follow-ups: NET-457 (vendor deep-dive), RUNTIME-783 (prefetch backpressure), SRE-221 (runbook update for drain+failover).

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-2345 status changed to "Mitigating".

elena: small operational note: if we see OOMs after node reboots, escalate to host reboot instead of container restart to clear driver-level RDMA state. saw stale QPs persist across container restarts once.

tom: confirmed nodal logs: `rdma_cm: QP state error: -110` persists until QPs cleared or host driver restarted. Will document.

support-bot: Final customer update queued: "Mitigation applied; performance improving. We'll follow with a detailed postmortem and timeline." Send in 30m?

raj: agreed. I'll keep monitoring for 1 hour and then start assembling timeline for postmortem. If anyone sees re-occurence ping me directly. :eyes:

elena: thanks team — handing off. :white_check_mark:

maya: adding reaction :thumbsup: and saving logs to evidence bucket at `s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-2345/logs/`

jordan: filing incident ticket with initial notes.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-2345 acknowledged by raj."
